name: phd-caps-unapproved
description: Interface review R3 (2026-09-18): the twin of phd-4xxxx-overuse and phd-noncse-cap with NOTHING attested. Both §4.2 allowances quote the same condition on their own cards — “subject to approval of the student's advisor and DGS” — so while a course is waiting for that approval neither row may read Met. The CSE-4xxxx cap used to; the non-CSE cap already did not, and a student with an unapproved course of either kind now gets the same verdict for the same situation. Nine credits of CSE 4xxxx against a six-credit cap and twelve non-CSE credits against a nine-credit cap, so each row also carries its over-cap line: the 4xxxx credits over the limit are lost (§4.2), the non-CSE credits over it still count toward the total (decision F1, 2026-09-12). (Sheet fidelity: this turns on the Courses tab's `counts_toward_phd = dgs_approval` cell, and since the 2026-09-18 re-pointing it turns on real live ones — CSE 40243, CSE 40437 and CSE 40567 each carry that verdict on the live sheet and the fixture copies their cells. It is the common shape: 160 of the live sheet's 181 CSE 4xxxx rows read `dgs_approval` for the Ph.D. in the 2026-09-16 snapshot, so this row's verdict is what most Ph.D. students with a 40000-level course will actually see.)

detailIncludes: 6 of the 6 credits below the 60000 level used

9 of the 9 non-CSE cap credits used
